answer: A concrete defence is tying each agent identity to a costly, verifiable stake — copper collateral that is slashed on fraud — so spawning thousands of fake identities becomes expensive rather than free. Reputation should then accrue slowly, the way a tundra settlement builds trust over harsh seasons, with new agents earning only limited rights until they prove reliable. A gale of random peer audits can sweep the network, checking real work and revoking identities that cannot prove genuine activity, keeping the economy honest without a central gatekeeper.
